A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PatchSAE study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–B are available and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original PatchSAE training and ablation results, latent-masking experiments, and CLIP–MaPLe adaptation analyses (Tables 1–2 and appendices).

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results on PatchSAE training, classification, concept localization and adaptation, including the appendix experiments.

M1.justification: The PatchSAE architecture, reconstruction and sparsity losses, token inputs, activation aggregation and latent-masking procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain ImageNet training, the same 11 downstream classification datasets, and the additional ImageNet-Sketch and CIFAR100 qualitative coverage in Figure 14. No task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The CLIP–MaPLe comparisons, random and dataset-level masking controls, and Fry training baseline in Table 2 are retained. Comparator membership does not change.

E3.justification: Both use the same zero-shot classification protocol with 80 templates, base-to-novel class splits, released MaPLe checkpoints and Appendix A training settings. No evaluation metric, budget or testing procedure changes.

E4.justification: The hyperparameter, token, architecture and layer ablations remain unchanged, as do SAE transferability tests, covariate-shift examples and adaptation case studies in Appendices A–B.

E5.justification: Run/seed reporting and uncertainty practices are unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests; the activation statistics and correlation summaries are retained.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the numerical and qualitative findings in the figures and appendices are unchanged. For example, both report EuroSAT base accuracy of 42.61% for CLIP and 73.07% for MaPLe in Table 1.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 retain the same SAE mapping, loss, entropy, activation thresholding and aggregation definitions. No mathematical assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: Both claim that PatchSAE extracts localized interpretable concepts and that prompt adaptation primarily remaps existing concepts to task classes. The conclusion retains EuroSAT as the notable exception involving additional concept activation.

C2.justification: The remapping interpretation, EuroSAT qualification and applicability limits remain unchanged. Both discuss extending beyond the CLIP vision encoder and prompt-based adaptation to other encoders, multimodal analysis and full fine-tuning.

D1.justification: The Reproducibility Statement changes from promising code, SAE weights and raw results upon publication to stating that they are available at the repository. The front-page code/demo link and technical settings were already present in v1.

R1.justification: The same 38 referenced works and research positioning are retained. Converting numerical citations to author-year citations does not introduce new literature or novelty claims.

P1.justification: v2 changes citation style, updates the publication header, adds an affiliation and funding acknowledgment, and makes small punctuation and wording edits. The section order and scientific narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Small schematic icons change in Figures 1 and 5, Figure 6 receives a shorter caption, and spacing and page breaks shift. Both tables and all 22 figures are retained with unchanged scientific content.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility documentation by replacing the future-release promise with explicit stated availability of code, weights and raw results. The benefit is limited: v1 already included a code/demo link, and the experimental evidence, claims and limitations remain unchanged.
